title: Company convocation slate and OKR hypotheses v0.1
content:
Purpose
---
This doc is an early working slate for the company-wide convocation (all-team huddle) and the OKR hypotheses we plan to surface to exec and leads. Goal is to create a compact set of asks and measurable experiments for the next 12 weeks that leaders can take to their teams.

Tone and constraints
- Lightweight, decision-oriented. Not a product spec.
- Focus on outcomes that improve inference economics (latency/cost/reliability) and unblock landing customers for Dedicated/Private.
- Timeboxed: we want a clear set of ownerable experiments, not a laundry list.

North star for convocation
- Align around 3 cross-org outcome bets that materially change our S-curve over the next quarter: 1) Increase revenue from Dedicated pipeline, 2) Reduce median-hosted latency P50 by 15% for top 5 models, 3) Cut per-token unit cost by 12% across common workloads.

Proposed OKR hypotheses (draft)
OKR 1: Grow Dedicated ARR and shorten sales cycle
- Objective: Demonstrably accelerate Dedicated deals and reduce implementation time
- Key results (hypotheses):
  - KR1.1: +30% in MRR from Dedicated pilot conversions vs baseline (12-week window)
  - KR1.2: Reduce average Dedicated onboarding time from 55 -> 35 days
  - KR1.3: Ship 2 turnkey integration templates (SFDC, Okta) and one solution brief used in at least 4 sales cycles
- Primary owners: Solutions Eng (Samir), GTM (Priya)
- Leading indicators to track: number of pilot installs, time to first successful inference, blocker categories (network, infra, security)

OKR 2: Improve hosted inference economics and SLOs
- Objective: Make hosted API noticeably cheaper and faster for typical app patterns
- Key results (hypotheses):
  - KR2.1: Median P50 latency for top 5 models drops 15% on average during peak traffic windows
  - KR2.2: Average per-token cost (hosted) drops 12% for 4 canonical workloads (chat, embeddings, rerank, completions)
  - KR2.3: Introduce a cache-aware SDK option and achieve 10% prefix reuse on production traffic for sampled customers
- Primary owners: Serving runtime (Ethan), Optimize (Maya)
- Important experiments: aggressive KV cache rollout, dynamic batching policy changes, new kernel toggles behind feature flags

OKR 3: Trust and enterprise enablement for Private deployments
- Objective: Remove friction for regulated customers and make Private a predictable customer motion
- Key results (hypotheses):
  - KR3.1: Close 3 new Private deployments (VPC or on-prem) with pre-signed contracts
  - KR3.2: Reduce time-to-deploy (customer-ready) from 28 -> 14 days for standard VPC flow
  - KR3.3: Add KMS/HSM integration pattern and one audit-playbook for SOC-like reviews
- Primary owners: Private deployments (Priya), Security & Compliance (Maya)

All-hands run of show (tentative, 90 min)
- 0:00–0:05 — Welcome, context & desired outcomes (CEO)
- 0:05–0:20 — Product pulse: serving runtime wins, Dedicated momentum, Private highlights (VP Product)
- 0:20–0:35 — Exec quickfire: three cross-org bets and what success looks like (3 x 5min)
- 0:35–0:55 — Breakout orientation: 3 rooms (Dedicated ops, Hosted performance, Private & compliance). Leaders set 3 team-level experiments to commit to.
- 0:55–1:10 — Live rollup: chosen experiments; triage of high-risk blockers
- 1:10–1:20 — Closing asks and next steps (Comms + tactical owners)
- 1:20–1:30 — Optional open Q&A / Slack pulse

Pre-meeting prep (for leads)
- Bring 1 measurable experiment that aligns to one of the OKR hypotheses and can be started within 2 weeks. Define owner, success metric, expected blockers, and resource ask (if any).
- Upload a 1-slide summary to the shared agenda (github link in linked artifacts) 48 hours prior.

Risk register (top-of-mind)
- Risk A: Competing infra priorities push batching/cache work down backlog and we miss latency/cost KRs. Mitigation: carve 20% sprint capacity across serving runtime for flagged experiments.
- Risk B: Sales motion for Dedicated limited by integration cadence. Mitigation: pre-build 2 integration templates and run 2 pilot sprints with Solutions Eng.
- Risk C: Private deployments hit compliance edge-cases. Mitigation: create a concise audit playbook and a 'fast-fail' checklist for non-standard controls.

Decision points for execs (items to sign off before convocation)
1) Approve prioritization: allocate an extra 0.5 FTE of infra engineering capacity for 8 weeks to support KR2 experiments.
2) Authorize two integration engineering sprints (4 weeks total) and a solutions eng pilot for Dedicated templates.
3) Endorse the audit playbook scope (Security to circulate draft by 2024-11-08).

Open questions / notes to self (working)
- Which canonical workloads should be the baseline for cost comparisons? (suggestion: chat + embeddings + long-context completions)
- Can we instrument a quick sample of 5 paying customers to measure prefix reuse today? Who owns access?
- Need a concise comms narrative for customers about temporary performance tuning changes (clear rollback language).

Immediate next steps (this week)
- Ethan: prototype a feature-flagged KV cache rollout on canary (due 2024-11-15).
- Samir + Priya: draft two integration templates and a one-pager for sales playbook (due 2024-11-19).
- Maya: circulate audit-playbook skeleton and list of required artifacts for SOC review (due 2024-11-08).
- Ava: finalize convocation logistics and invite list; publish slide template for leads (due 2024-11-10).

Communication plan
- Pre-read (short): 2-page convocation brief + slide template (to be posted to Confluence link in linked_artifacts).
- Follow-up: post-event rollup with experiment commitments and owner tracker (biweekly sync cadence).

Appendix: quick metrics to include in pre-read (placeholders)
- Current Dedicated pipeline MRR: $1.2M (ARR run-rate ~ $14.4M)
- Median hosted P50 latency (top 5 models): 72ms
- Current per-token hosted unit cost (canonical workloads): $0.0018/token
- Average Dedicated onboarding time: 55 days

Sidenotes (informal)
- Keep breakout rooms pragmatic — prefer live commitments over huge whiteboard sessions.
- Encourage leads to write down 1 risk and 1 mitigation per experiment before the breakouts.

If you want to iterate on the OKR wording I can convert these into a single-slide OKR sheet per hypothesis and push to the shared agenda.

-- Ava
